sanskrit: sa tu dattvā daśagrīvo vanaṃ ghoraṃ kharasya tat bhaginīṃ ca samāśvāsya hṛṣṭaḥ svasthataro 'bhavat
english: Having given that dreadful forest to Khara and having comforted his sister, the ten-necked one grew cheerful and yet more at ease.

sanskrit: tato nikumbhilā nāma laṅkāyāḥ kānanaṃ mahat mahātmā rākṣasendras tat praviveśa sahānugaḥ
english: Then the great-souled lord of the Rākṣasas entered together with his retinue that great grove of Laṅkā called Nikumbhilā.

sanskrit: tatra yūpaśatākīrṇaṃ saumyacaityopaśobhitam dadarśa viṣṭhitaṃ yajñaṃ saṃpradīptam iva śriyā
english: There he saw a sacrifice in progress, strewn with hundreds of sacrificial posts and adorned with graceful altars, blazing as it were with sacred splendour.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ kamaṇḍaluśikhādhvajam dadarśa svasutaṃ tatra meghanādam ariṃdamam
english: There he saw his own son Meghanāda, the subduer of enemies, wearing a black antelope-skin and bearing the water-pot and sacrificial fire as his banner.

sanskrit: rakṣaḥpatiḥ samāsādya samāśliṣya ca bāhubhiḥ abravīt kim idaṃ vatsa vartate tad bravīhi me
english: The lord of the Rākṣasas approached him, embraced him with his arms, and said: "What is this that is going on, my son? Tell me."

sanskrit: uśanā tv abravīt tatra gurur yajñasamṛddhaye rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasaśreṣṭhaṃ dvijaśreṣṭho mahātapāḥ
english: Then Uśanas, the preceptor, that foremost of twice-born sages possessed of great austerity, spoke to Rāvaṇa, the foremost of Rākṣasas, for the sake of the success of the sacrifice:

sanskrit: aham ākhyāmi te rājañ śrūyatāṃ sarvam eva ca yajñās te sapta putreṇa prāptāḥ subahuvistarāḥ
english: "I shall tell you, O king — hear everything in full. Your son has accomplished seven sacrifices of great extent and detail.

sanskrit: agniṣṭomo 'śvamedhaś ca yajño bahusuvarṇakaḥ rājasūyas tathā yajño gomedho vaiṣṇavas tathā
english: The Agniṣṭoma, the Aśvamedha — the sacrifice rich in gold — the Rājasūya, the Gomedha, and the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice as well —

sanskrit: māheśvare pravṛtte tu yajñe pumbhiḥ sudurlabhe varāṃs te labdhavān putraḥ sākṣāt paśupater iha
english: — and during the performance of the Māheśvara sacrifice, so difficult for men to accomplish, your son has obtained boons here directly from the Lord of creatures Paśupati himself.

sanskrit: kāmagaṃ syandanaṃ divyaṃ antarikṣacaraṃ dhruvam māyāṃ ca tāmasīṃ nāma yayā saṃpadyate tamaḥ
english: A divine chariot that goes wherever one wishes, moving through the sky unfailingly, and the illusion named Tāmasī by which darkness is brought about —

sanskrit: etayā kila saṃgrāme māyayā rākṣaseśvara prayuddhasya gatiḥ śakyā na hi jñātuṃ surāsuraiḥ
english: — by this illusion, O lord of Rākṣasas, the movements of one fighting in battle cannot be discerned even by gods and Asuras.

sanskrit: akṣayāv iṣudhī bāṇaiś cāpaṃ cāpi sudurjayam astraṃ ca balavat saumya śatruvidhvaṃsanaṃ raṇe
english: Two inexhaustible quivers, arrows, and a bow most difficult to overcome, and a powerful weapon that destroys enemies in battle —

sanskrit: etān sarvān varāṃl labdhvā putras te 'yaṃ daśānana adya yajñasamāptau ca tvatpratīkṣaḥ sthito aham
english: — having obtained all these boons, this your son, O ten-faced one, has completed the sacrifice today, and I have remained here awaiting you."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd daśagrīvo na śobhanam idaṃ kṛtam pūjitāḥ śatravo yasmād dravyair indrapurogamāḥ
english: Then the ten-necked one said: "This has not been done well, for the enemies headed by Indra have been honoured with offerings.

sanskrit: ehīdānīṃ kṛtaṃ yad dhi tad akartuṃ na śakyate āgaccha saumya gacchāmaḥ svam eva bhavanaṃ prati
english: Come now — what has been done cannot be undone. Come, my gentle one; let us go to our own palace."

sanskrit: tato gatvā daśagrīvaḥ saputraḥ savibhīṣaṇaḥ striyo 'vatārayām āsa sarvās tā bāṣpaviklavāḥ
english: Then Daśagrīva, together with his son and Vibhīṣaṇa, went and caused all those women — all of them distressed with tears — to descend from their conveyances.

sanskrit: lakṣiṇyo ratnabūtāś ca devadānavarakṣasām nānābhūṣaṇasaṃpannā jvalantyaḥ svena tejasā
english: Auspicious and jewel-like women of gods, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, adorned with varied ornaments, blazing with their own radiance —

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu tā nārīr dṛṣṭvā śokasamākulāḥ tasya tāṃ ca matiṃ jñātvā dharmātmā vākyam abravīt
english: Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous in soul, seeing those women overcome with grief and knowing the mind of his brother, spoke these words:

sanskrit: īdṛśais taiḥ samācārair yaśo'rthakulanāśanaiḥ dharṣaṇaṃ prāṇināṃ dattvā svamatena viceṣṭase
english: "With such conduct as this — destructive of honour, purpose, and family — you act according to your own will, causing outrage to living beings.

sanskrit: jñātīn vai dharṣayitvemās tvayānītā varāṅganāḥ tvām atikramya madhunā rājan kumbhīnasī hṛtā
english: Having violated the kinswomen and brought these beautiful women here, Kumbhīnasī has been abducted by Madhu, transgressing against you, O king.

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tv abravīd vākyaṃ nāvagacchāmi kiṃ tv idam ko vāyaṃ yas tvayākhyāto madhur ity eva nāmataḥ
english: Rāvaṇa then said: "I do not understand — what is this? Who is this one whom you have named as Madhu?"

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu saṃkruddho bhrātaraṃ vākyam abravīt śrūyatām asya pāpasya karmaṇaḥ phalam āgatam
english: Vibhīṣaṇa, deeply angered, spoke to his brother: "Hear — the fruit of this sinful act has now arrived.

sanskrit: mātāmahasya yo 'smākaṃ jyeṣṭho bhrātā sumālinaḥ mālyavān iti vikhyāto vṛddhaprājño niśācaraḥ
english: The eldest brother of our maternal grandfather Sumālin, the night-wanderer known as Mālyavān, wise and aged —

sanskrit: pitur jyeṣṭho jananyāś ca asmākaṃ tv āryako 'bhavat tasya kumbhīnasī nāma duhitur duhitābhavat
english: — he was the eldest, the noble ancestor on our mother's and father's side; his daughter's daughter was named Kumbhīnasī.

sanskrit: mātṛṣvasur athāsmākaṃ sā kanyā cānalodbhavā bhavaty asmākam eṣā vai bhrātṝṇāṃ dharmataḥ svasā
english: That maiden born of fire is our mother's sister's child; she is thus by dharma a sister to us brothers.

sanskrit: sā hṛtā madhunā rājan rākṣasena balīyasā yajñapravṛtte putre te mayi cāntarjaloṣite
english: She has been abducted by Madhu, that powerful Rākṣasa, O king, while your son was engaged in the sacrifice and I too was preoccupied within the waters.

sanskrit: nihatya rākṣasaśreṣṭhān amātyāṃs tava saṃmatān dharṣayitvā hṛtā rājan guptā hy antaḥpure tava
english: Having slain the foremost Rākṣasas who were your trusted ministers, having violated her, he abducted her, O king — she who was under protection in your inner apartments.

sanskrit: śrutvā tv etan mahārāja kṣāntam eva hato na saḥ yasmād avaśyaṃ dātavyā kanyā bhartre hi dātṛbhiḥ asminn evābhisaṃprāptaṃ loke viditam astu te
english: "Having heard this, O great king, I endured — and he was not slain — because a maiden must inevitably be given by her givers to a husband. Let this be known and understood by you in respect of what has now come to pass."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd daśagrīvaḥ kruddhaḥ saṃraktalocanaḥ kalpyatāṃ me rathaḥ śīghraṃ śūrāḥ sajjībhavantu ca
english: Then Daśagrīva, enraged, his eyes red, said: "Let my chariot be made ready at once, and let the warriors equip themselves.

sanskrit: bhrātā me kumbhakarṇaś ca ye ca mukhyā niśācarāḥ vāhanāny adhirohantu nānāpraharaṇāyudhāḥ
english: My brother Kumbhakarṇa and the principal night-wanderers — let them mount their vehicles, armed with weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: adya taṃ samare hatvā madhuṃ rāvaṇanirbhayam indralokaṃ gamiṣyāmi yuddhakāṅkṣī suhṛdvṛtaḥ
english: Having slain that Madhu in battle today — Madhu who fears nothing before Rāvaṇa — I shall proceed to the world of Indra, eager for battle, surrounded by friends.

sanskrit: tato vijitya tridivaṃ vaśe sthāpya puraṃdaram nirvṛto vihariṣyāmi trailokyaiśvaryaśobhitaḥ
english: Then, having conquered the triple heaven and brought Purandara under my sway, I shall roam in contentment, glorified by sovereignty over the three worlds.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇīsahasrāṇi catvāry ugrāṇi rakṣasām nānāpraharaṇāny āśu niryayur yuddhakāṅkṣiṇām
english: Four thousand Akṣauhiṇī armies of fierce Rākṣasas bearing weapons of every kind quickly marched out, eager for battle.

sanskrit: indrajit tv agrataḥ sainyaṃ sainikān parigṛhya ca rāvaṇo madhyataḥ śūraḥ kumbhakarṇaś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Indrajit led the army at the vanguard marshalling the soldiers; the valiant Rāvaṇa was in the middle; and Kumbhakarṇa brought up the rear.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu dharmātmā laṅkāyāṃ dharmam ācarat te tu sarve mahābhāgā yayur madhupuraṃ prati
english: Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous in soul, remained in Laṅkā practising dharma, while all those great and illustrious ones marched toward the city of Madhu.

sanskrit: rathair nāgaiḥ kharair uṣṭrair hayair dīptair mahoragaiḥ rākṣasāḥ prayayuḥ sarve kṛtvākāśaṃ nirantaram
english: The Rākṣasas all advanced on chariots, elephants, donkeys, camels, swift horses, and great serpents, making the sky unbroken with their masses.

sanskrit: daityāś ca śataśas tatra kṛtavairāḥ suraiḥ saha rāvaṇaṃ prekṣya gacchantam anvagacchanta pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Hundreds of Daityas who had made enmity with the gods, seeing Rāvaṇa setting out, followed behind him.

sanskrit: sa tu gatvā madhupuraṃ praviśya ca daśānanaḥ na dadarśa madhuṃ tatra bhaginīṃ tatra dṛṣṭavān
english: But having gone and entered the city of Madhu, the ten-faced one did not find Madhu there; he found only his sister.

sanskrit: sā prahvā prāñjalir bhūtvā śirasā pādayor gatā tasya rākṣasarājasya trastā kumbhīnasī svasā
english: Trembling, Kumbhīnasī, the sister of that king of Rākṣasas, bowed with folded hands and cast herself at his feet with her head.

sanskrit: tāṃ samutthāpayām āsa na bhetavyam iti bruvan rāvaṇo rākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ cāpi karavāṇi te
english: Rāvaṇa, foremost of Rākṣasas, raised her up saying "Fear not", and added: "What shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: sābravīd yadi me rājan prasannas tvaṃ mahābala bhartāraṃ na mamehādya hantum arhasi mānada
english: She said: "If you are pleased with me, O king of great strength, O bestower of honour, then do not slay my husband here today.

sanskrit: satyavāg bhava rājendra mām avekṣasva yācatīm tvayā hy uktaṃ mahābāho na bhetavyam iti svayam
english: Be true to your word, O lord of kings — regard me as I beseech you; for you yourself said with your own lips, O mighty-armed one, 'Fear not.'"

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tv abravīd dhṛṣṭaḥ svasāraṃ tatra saṃsthitām kva cāsau tava bhartā vai mama śīghraṃ nivedyatām
english: Rāvaṇa then spoke boldly to his sister standing there: "Where is your husband? Let him be brought before me at once."

sanskrit: saha tena gamiṣyāmi suralokaṃ jayāya vai tava kāruṇyasauhārdān nivṛtto 'smi madhor vadhāt
english: "I shall go with him to the world of the gods for conquest. Out of compassion and affection for you, I have turned back from slaying Madhu."

sanskrit: ity uktā sā prasuptaṃ taṃ samutthāpya niśācaram abravīt saṃprahṛṣṭeva rākṣasī suvipaścitam
english: Thus addressed, she, the Rākṣasī, woke the sleeping night-wanderer and spoke these wise words as if with joy:

sanskrit: eṣa prāpto daśagrīvo mama bhrātā niśācaraḥ suralokajayākāṅkṣī sāhāyye tvāṃ vṛṇoti ca
english: "My brother, the ten-necked night-wanderer, has arrived, desiring to conquer the world of the gods; he chooses you for his ally.

sanskrit: tad asya tvaṃ sahāyārthaṃ sabandhur gaccha rākṣasa snigdhasya bhajamānasya yuktam arthāya kalpitum
english: Therefore go together with your kinsmen to serve as his ally, O Rākṣasa — it is fitting to serve the purpose of one who is devoted and affectionate."

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā tathety āha madhur vacaḥ dadarśa rākṣasaśreṣṭhaṃ yathānyāyam upetya saḥ
english: Hearing her words, Madhu said "So be it" and, approaching in due form, met the foremost of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: pūjayām āsa dharmeṇa rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam prāptapūjo daśagrīvo madhuveśmani vīryavān tatra caikāṃ niśām uṣya gamanāyopacakrame
english: He honoured Rāvaṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas, according to the rites of hospitality; the valiant ten-necked one, having received due honour in the dwelling of Madhu and having spent one night there, set out once more on his journey.

sanskrit: tataḥ kailāsam āsādya śailaṃ vaiśravaṇālayam rākṣasendro mahendrābhaḥ senām upaniveśayat
english: Then the lord of Rākṣasas, resplendent as Mahendra, reached Mount Kailāsa, the abode of Vaiśravaṇa, and encamped his army.

sanskrit: sa tu tatra daśagrīvaḥ saha sainyena vīryavān astaṃ prāpte dinakare nivāsaṃ samarocayat
english: The valiant Daśagrīva, having arrived there with his army, chose a camp as the sun was setting.

sanskrit: udite vimale candre tulyaparvatavarcasi sa dadarśa guṇāṃs tatra candrapādopaśobhitān
english: When the pure moon rose, equal in splendour to a great mountain, he beheld in that place virtues and beauties illuminated by the moon's beams.

sanskrit: karṇikāravanair divyaiḥ kadambagahanais tathā padminībhiś ca phullābhir mandākinyā jalair api
english: Divine groves of Karṇikāra trees and dense clusters of Kadamba, lotus-ponds in full bloom, and the waters of the Mandākinī —

sanskrit: ghaṇṭānām iva saṃnādaḥ śuśruve madhurasvanaḥ apsarogaṇasaṃghanāḥ gāyatāṃ dhanadālaye
english: — a sweet sound like the ringing of bells was heard — the mingled voices of throngs of Apsarasas singing in the abode of Dhanada.

sanskrit: puṣpavarṣāṇi muñcanto nagāḥ pavanatāḍitāḥ śailaṃ taṃ vāsayantīva madhumādhavagandhinaḥ
english: Trees shaken by the wind poured showers of flowers, as if perfuming that mountain with the fragrance of honey and spring blossoms.

sanskrit: madhupuṣparajaḥpṛktaṃ gandham ādāya puṣkalam pravavau vardhayan kāmaṃ rāvaṇasya sukho 'nilaḥ
english: The pleasant breeze blew, carrying an abundant fragrance mingled with the pollen of honey-flowers, kindling desire in Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: geyāt puṣpasamṛddhyā ca śaityād vāyor guṇair gireḥ pravṛttāyāṃ rajanyāṃ ca candrasyodayanena ca
english: By the abundance of song and blossoms, by the coolness of the breeze, by the virtues of the mountain, by the advancing night, and by the rising of the moon —

sanskrit: rāvaṇaḥ sumahāvīryaḥ kāmabāṇavaśaṃ gataḥ viniśvasya viniśvasya śaśinaṃ samavaikṣata
english: — Rāvaṇa of very great prowess came under the sway of Kāma's arrows and, sighing again and again, gazed upon the moon.

sanskrit: etasminn antare tatra divyapuṣpavibhūṣitā sarvāpsarovarā rambhā pūrṇacandranibhānanā
english: At that moment there appeared Rambhā, the foremost of all Apsarasas, adorned with divine flowers, her face like the full moon —

sanskrit: kṛtair viśeṣakair ārdraiḥ ṣaḍartukusumotsavaiḥ nīlaṃ satoyameghābhaṃ vastraṃ samavaguṇṭhitā
english: — wearing fresh beauty-marks and garlands of blossoms from the festival of all six seasons, wrapped in a garment dark as a rain-bearing cloud —

sanskrit: yasya vaktraṃ śaśinibhaṃ bhruvau cāpanibhe śubhe ūrū karikarākārau karau pallavakomalau sainyamadhyena gacchantī rāvaṇenopalakṣitā
english: — whose face was like the moon, whose beautiful brows were like bows, whose thighs were like the trunks of elephants, and whose hands were soft as young leaves — she was noticed by Rāvaṇa as she walked through the midst of the army.

sanskrit: tāṃ samutthāya rakṣendraḥ kāmabāṇabalārditaḥ kare gṛhītvā gacchantīṃ smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: The lord of Rākṣasas rose and, overpowered by the force of Kāma's arrow, seized her by the hand as she passed, and smiling, spoke to her:

sanskrit: kva gacchasi varārohe kāṃ siddhiṃ bhajase svayam kasyābhyudayakālo 'yaṃ yas tvāṃ samupabhokṣyate
english: "Where do you go, O lovely one? What fulfilment do you seek of your own will? Whose auspicious hour is this — he who will enjoy you?

sanskrit: tavānanarasasyādya padmotpalasugandhinaḥ sudhāmṛtarasasyeva ko 'dya tṛptiṃ gamiṣyati
english: Today, of the juice of your face — fragrant with lotus and blue water-lily, like the taste of nectar and immortal elixir — who today will drink his fill?

sanskrit: svarṇakumbhanibhau pīnau śubhau bhīru nirantarau kasyorasthalasaṃsparśaṃ dāsyatas te kucāv imau
english: Your two breasts, round and auspicious as golden jars, set close together, O timid one — on whose chest will they bestow their touch?

sanskrit: suvarṇacakrapratimaṃ svarṇadāmacitaṃ pṛthu adhyārokṣyati kas te 'dya svargaṃ jaghanarūpiṇam
english: Who today will mount your broad hips, like heaven in form, resembling a golden wheel and wreathed with a golden girdle?

sanskrit: madviśiṣṭaḥ pumān ko 'nyaḥ śakro viṣṇur athāśvinau mām atītya hi yasya tvaṃ yāsi bhīru na śobhanam
english: What man is there superior to me — Śakra, Viṣṇu, or the Aśvins? It is not fitting, O timid one, that you pass me by to go to anyone.

sanskrit: viśrama tvaṃ pṛthuśroṇi śilātalam idaṃ śubham trailokye yaḥ prabhuś caiva tulyo mama na vidyate
english: Rest yourself, O broad-hipped one, on this auspicious stone floor. There is no sovereign in all three worlds who is my equal.

sanskrit: tad eṣa prāñjaliḥ prahvo yācate tvāṃ daśānanaḥ yaḥ prabhuś cāpi bhartā ca trailokyasya bhajasva mām
english: Therefore this Daśagrīva, who is the lord and master of the three worlds, with folded hands and bowed head, implores you — accept me."

sanskrit: evam uktābravīd rambhā vepamānā kṛtāñjaliḥ prasīda nārhase vaktum īdṛśaṃ tvaṃ hi me guruḥ
english: Thus addressed, Rambhā, trembling, spoke with folded hands: "Be gracious. You ought not to speak thus — you are my elder and guardian.

sanskrit: anyebhyo 'pi tvayā rakṣyā prāpnuyāṃ dharṣaṇaṃ yadi dharmataś ca snuṣā te 'haṃ tattvam etad bravīmi te
english: I should be protected by you even from others; were I to suffer violation, I tell you in truth that by dharma I am your daughter-in-law.

sanskrit: abravīt tāṃ daśagrīvaś caraṇādhomukhīṃ sthitām sutasya yadi me bhāryā tatas tvaṃ me snuṣā bhaveḥ
english: Daśagrīva spoke to her as she stood looking downward at his feet: "If you are the wife of my son, then you would be my daughter-in-law.

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva sā rambhā prāha rāvaṇam uttaram dharmatas te sutasyāhaṃ bhāryā rākṣasapuṃgava
english: Rambhā replied to Rāvaṇa: "Truly so — by dharma I am the wife of your son, O foremost of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: putraḥ priyataraḥ prāṇair bhrātur vaiśravaṇasya te khyāto yas triṣu lokeṣu nalakūbara ity asau
english: He is a son more dear than life to your brother Vaiśravaṇa — he who is renowned in all three worlds as Nalakūbara.

sanskrit: dharmato yo bhaved vipraḥ kṣatriyo vīryato bhavet krodhād yaś ca bhaved agniḥ kṣāntyā ca vasudhāsamaḥ
english: He who is a Brāhmaṇa by virtue of dharma, a Kṣatriya by virtue of valour, who is like fire in wrath and like the earth in patience —

sanskrit: tasyāsmi kṛtasaṃketā lokapālasutasya vai tam uddiśya ca me sarvaṃ vibhūṣaṇam idaṃ kṛtam
english: — of him, the son of the world-guardian, I have made a tryst; for him alone all this adornment of mine has been made.

sanskrit: yasya tasya hi nānyasya bhāvo māṃ prati tiṣṭhati tena satyena māṃ rājan moktum arhasy ariṃdama
english: His love and no other's rests upon me — by that truth, O king, O subduer of enemies, you ought to release me.

sanskrit: sa hi tiṣṭhati dharmātmā sāmprataṃ matsamutsukaḥ tan na vighnaṃ sutasyeha kartum arhasi muñca mām
english: He, the righteous-souled one, is now waiting in longing for me — therefore you ought not to create an obstacle here for your son's beloved. Release me."

sanskrit: sadbhir ācaritaṃ mārgaṃ gaccha rākṣasapuṃgava mānanīyo mayā hi tvaṃ lālanīyā tathāsmi te
english: "Follow the path trodden by the virtuous, O foremost of Rākṣasas; you are to be honoured by me, and I am to be cherished by you."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇāṃ rambhāṃ tāṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ nirbhartsya rākṣaso mohāt pratigṛhya balād balī kāmamohābhisaṃrabdho maithunāyopacakrame
english: Though Rambhā spoke these words full of dharma and reason, the powerful Rākṣasa, scorning them, and overcome by the infatuation of lust, seized her by force and proceeded to violate her.

sanskrit: sā vimuktā tato rambhā bhraṣṭamālyavibhūṣaṇā gajendrākrīḍamathitā nadīvākulatāṃ gatā
english: Rambhā, thus freed, her garlands and ornaments fallen away, was thrown into confusion like a river disturbed by a bull elephant at play.

sanskrit: sā vepamānā lajjantī bhītā karakṛtāñjaliḥ nalakūbaram āsādya pādayor nipapāta ha
english: Trembling, filled with shame and fear, she came to Nalakūbara with joined hands and fell at his feet.

sanskrit: tadavasthāṃ ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmā nalakūbaraḥ abravīt kim idaṃ bhadre pādayoḥ patitāsi me
english: Seeing her in that condition, the great-souled Nalakūbara said: "What is this, dear one? Why have you fallen at my feet?"

sanskrit: sā tu niśvasamānā ca vepamānātha sāñjaliḥ tasmai sarvaṃ yathātathyam ākhyātum upacakrame
english: She, sighing and trembling, her hands joined, proceeded to tell him everything exactly as it had happened.

sanskrit: eṣa deva daśagrīvaḥ prāpto gantuṃ triviṣṭapam tena sainyasahāyena niśeha pariṇāmyate
english: "This Daśagrīva, O god, has come intending to go to heaven; the night here is being passed with the help of his army.

sanskrit: āyāntī tena dṛṣṭāsmi tvatsakāśam ariṃdama gṛhītvā tena pṛṣṭāsmi kasya tvam iti rakṣasā
english: As I was coming toward you, I was seen by him, O subduer of enemies; that Rākṣasa seized me and asked me 'Whose are you?'

sanskrit: mayā tu sarvaṃ yat satyaṃ tad dhi tasmai niveditam kāmamohābhibhūtātmā nāśrauṣīt tad vaco mama
english: I told him the whole truth, but his mind overwhelmed by the delusion of desire did not heed those words of mine.

sanskrit: yācyamāno mayā deva snuṣā te 'ham iti prabho tat sarvaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā balāt tenāsmi dharṣitā
english: Though I implored him saying 'I am your daughter-in-law, O lord,' he cast all that aside and violated me by force.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvam aparādhaṃ me kṣantum arhasi mānada na hi tulyaṃ balaṃ saumya striyāś ca puruṣasya ca
english: Thus you should forgive this transgression against me, O bestower of honour; for the strength of a woman is in no way equal to that of a man, O gentle one."

sanskrit: evaṃ śrutvā tu saṃkruddhas tadā vaiśvaraṇātmajaḥ dharṣaṇāṃ tāṃ parāṃ śrutvā dhyānaṃ saṃpraviveśa ha
english: Hearing this, the son of Vaiśravaṇa became deeply enraged; having heard of that great outrage, he fell into meditation.

sanskrit: tasya tat karma vijñāya tadā vaiśravaṇātmajaḥ muhūrtād roṣatāmrākṣas toyaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā
english: Understanding that deed fully, the son of Vaiśravaṇa, his eyes red with wrath after a moment, took water in his hand.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā salilaṃ divyam upaspṛśya yathāvidhi utsasarja tadā śāpaṃ rākṣasendrāya dāruṇam
english: Taking that divine water and touching it in the prescribed manner, he then pronounced a dreadful curse upon the lord of Rākṣasas:

sanskrit: akāmā tena yasmāt tvaṃ balād bhadre pradharṣitā tasmāt sa yuvatīm anyāṃ nākāmām upayāsyati
english: "Because he has violated you, dear one, by force when you were unwilling, therefore he shall never approach another young woman who is unwilling.

sanskrit: yadā tv akāmāṃ kāmārto dharṣayiṣyati yoṣitam mūrdhā tu saptadhā tasya śakalībhavitā tadā
english: When, overcome by desire, he shall violate a woman who is unwilling, his head shall then split into seven pieces."

sanskrit: tasminn udāhṛte śāpe jvalitāgnisamaprabhe devadundubhayo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiś ca khāc cyutā
english: When that curse blazing like a lit fire was pronounced, the divine kettledrums resounded and a rain of flowers fell from the sky.

sanskrit: prajāpatimukhāś cāpi sarve devāḥ praharṣitāḥ jñātvā lokagatiṃ sarvāṃ tasya mṛtyuṃ ca rakṣasaḥ
english: All the gods with Prajāpati at their head rejoiced greatly, knowing the entire course of the worlds and the death of that Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu sa daśagrīvas taṃ śāpaṃ romaharṣaṇam nārīṣu maithunaṃ bhāvaṃ nākāmāsv abhyarocayat
english: Hearing that hair-raising curse, Daśagrīva no longer delighted in the thought of sexual union with women who were unwilling.

sanskrit: kailāsaṃ laṅghayitvātha daśagrīvaḥ sarākṣasaḥ āsasāda mahātejā indralokaṃ niśācaraḥ
english: Having crossed Kailāsa, the ten-necked night-wanderer of great splendour advanced with his Rākṣasas and reached the world of Indra.

sanskrit: tasya rākṣasasainyasya samantād upayāsyataḥ devalokaṃ yayau śabdo bhidyamānārṇavopamaḥ
english: As his Rākṣasa army advanced on all sides toward the world of the gods, a sound arose like the crashing of the ocean at dissolution.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu rāvaṇaṃ prāptam indraḥ saṃcalitāsanaḥ abravīt tatra tān devān sarvān eva samāgatān
english: Hearing that Rāvaṇa had arrived, Indra rose from his seat and addressed all the gods who had assembled there:

sanskrit: ādityān savasūn rudrān viśvān sādhyān marudgaṇān sajjībhavata yuddhārthaṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
english: "Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvas, Sādhyas, and the hosts of Maruts — equip yourselves for battle against the wicked Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: evam uktās tu śakreṇa devāḥ śakrasamā yudhi saṃnahyanta mahāsattvā yuddhaśraddhāsamanvitāḥ
english: Thus addressed by Śakra, the gods, equal to Śakra in battle, great-souled, filled with eagerness for the fight, armed themselves.

sanskrit: sa tu dīnaḥ paritrasto mahendro rāvaṇaṃ prati viṣṇoḥ samīpam āgatya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: But Mahendra, distressed and frightened before Rāvaṇa, came to Viṣṇu and spoke these words:

sanskrit: viṣṇo kathaṃ kariṣyāmo mahāvīryaparākrama asau hi balavān rakṣo yuddhārtham abhivartate
english: "O Viṣṇu of great prowess and valour, what shall we do? That Rākṣasa is powerful and advances intent on battle.

sanskrit: varapradānād balavān na khalv anyena hetunā tac ca satyaṃ hi kartavyaṃ vākyaṃ deva prajāpateḥ
english: He is powerful by virtue of boons granted — not for any other reason. And the word of Prajāpati must indeed be honoured, O god.

sanskrit: tad yathā namucir vṛtro balir narakaśambarau tvan mataṃ samavaṣṭabhya yathā dagdhās tathā kuru
english: Therefore, as Namuci, Vṛtra, Bali, Naraka, and Śambara were burnt by relying on your intent, so act now.

sanskrit: na hy anyo deva devānām āpatsu sumahābala gatiḥ parāyaṇaṃ vāsti tvām ṛte puruṣottama
english: For in calamities, O god of great strength, the gods have no other recourse or refuge apart from you, O Puruṣottama.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān padmanābhaḥ sanātanaḥ tvayāhaṃ sthāpitaś caiva devarājye sanātane
english: You are Nārāyaṇa the glorious, Padmanābha the eternal; it was by you that I was established in the eternal kingship of the gods.

sanskrit: tad ākhyāhi yathātattvaṃ devadeva mama svayam asicakrasahāyas tvaṃ yudhyase saṃyuge ripum
english: Therefore tell me in truth yourself, O god of gods — do you, aided by your sword and discus, fight the enemy in battle?"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa śakreṇa devo nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ abravīn na paritrāsaḥ kāryas te śrūyatāṃ ca me
english: Thus addressed by Śakra, the lord god Nārāyaṇa replied: "No fear need be entertained by you. Hear my words.

sanskrit: na tāvad eṣa durvṛttaḥ śakyo daivatadānavaiḥ hantuṃ yudhi samāsādya varadānena durjayaḥ
english: This miscreant cannot be slain in battle by gods or Dānavas, being unconquerable by virtue of the boons he has received.

sanskrit: sarvathā tu mahat karma kariṣyati balotkaṭaḥ rakṣaḥ putrasahāyo 'sau dṛṣṭam etan nisargataḥ
english: Yet this Rākṣasa of excessive strength, aided by his son, will in any case accomplish great deeds — this is seen by natural fate.

sanskrit: bravīṣi yat tu māṃ śakra saṃyuge yotsyasīti ha naivāhaṃ pratiyotsye taṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: As for what you say to me — 'Will you fight in battle?' — I shall not fight that Rāvaṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: anihatya ripuṃ viṣṇur na hi pratinivartate durlabhaś caiṣa kāmo 'dya varam āsādya rākṣase
english: Viṣṇu does not turn back without slaying the enemy; yet today this wish is difficult to fulfil while the Rākṣasa possesses his boon.

sanskrit: pratijānāmi devendra tvatsamīpaṃ śatakrato rākṣasasyāham evāsya bhavitā mṛtyukāraṇam
english: I promise you, O Devendra, O Śatakratu — I alone will be the cause of the death of this Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: aham enaṃ vadhiṣyāmi rāvaṇaṃ sasutaṃ yudhi devatās toṣayiṣyāmi jñātvā kālam upasthitam
english: I will slay Rāvaṇa together with his sons in battle and satisfy the gods, knowing the appointed time has arrived."

sanskrit: etasminn antare nādaḥ śuśruve rajanīkṣaye tasya rāvaṇasainyasya prayuddhasya samantataḥ
english: In that interval, at the close of night, a mighty roar was heard on all sides from the army of Rāvaṇa as it engaged in battle.

sanskrit: atha yuddhaṃ samabhavad devarākṣasayos tadā ghoraṃ tumulanirhrādaṃ nānāpraharaṇāyudham
english: Then a battle broke out between the gods and the Rākṣasas — dreadful, with a tumultuous uproar and weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: etasminn antare śūrā rākṣasā ghoradarśanāḥ yuddhārtham abhyadhāvanta sacivā rāvaṇājñayā
english: Meanwhile the valiant, fearsome-looking Rākṣasa ministers rushed forward for battle at Rāvaṇa's command.

sanskrit: mārīcaś ca prahastaś ca mahāpārśvamahodarau akampano nikumbhaś ca śukaḥ sāraṇa eva ca
english: Mārīca, Prahasta, Mahāpārśva, Mahodara, Akampana, Nikumbha, Śuka, and Sāraṇa —

sanskrit: saṃhrādir dhūmaketuś ca mahādaṃṣṭro mahāmukhaḥ jambumālī mahāmālī virūpākṣaś ca rākṣasaḥ
english: — Saṃhrādi, Dhūmaketu, Mahādaṃṣṭra, Mahāmukha, Jambumālī, Mahāmālī, and the Rākṣasa Virūpākṣa —

sanskrit: etaiḥ sarvair mahāvīryair vṛto rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ rāvaṇasyāryakaḥ sainyaṃ sumālī praviveśa ha
english: — surrounded by all these warriors of great valour, Sumālī, the noble ancestor of Rāvaṇa, the foremost Rākṣasa, entered the army.

sanskrit: sa hi devagaṇān sarvān nānāpraharaṇaiḥ śitaiḥ vidhvaṃsayati saṃkruddhaḥ saha taiḥ kṣaṇadācaraiḥ
english: He, enraged, together with those night-wanderers, scattered all the hosts of gods with sharp weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: etasminn antare śūro vasūnām aṣṭamo vasuḥ sāvitra iti vikhyātaḥ praviveśa mahāraṇam
english: At that moment the valiant eighth of the Vasus, known as Sāvitra, entered the great battle.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavat surāṇāṃ rākṣasaiḥ saha kruddhānāṃ rakṣasāṃ kīrtiṃ samareṣv anivartinām
english: Then a battle broke out between the gods and the Rākṣasas — those Rākṣasas of renown, never retreating in combat.

sanskrit: tatas te rākṣasāḥ śūrā devāṃs tān samare sthitān nānāpraharaṇair ghorais jaghnuḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Then those valiant Rākṣasas struck down the gods standing in battle by hundreds of thousands with dreadful weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: surās tu rākṣasān ghorān mahāvīryān svatejasā samare vividhaiḥ śastrair anayan yamasādanam
english: But the gods in turn dispatched the fearsome, mighty Rākṣasas to the abode of Yama in battle with their own valour and various weapons.

sanskrit: etasminn antare śūraḥ sumālī nāma rākṣasaḥ nānāpraharaṇaiḥ kruddho raṇam evābhyavartata
english: At that moment the valiant Rākṣasa named Sumālī, enraged, advanced upon the battlefield with weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: devānāṃ tad balaṃ sarvaṃ nānāpraharaṇaiḥ śitaiḥ vidhvaṃsayati saṃkruddho vāyur jaladharān iva
english: Enraged, he scattered the entire force of the gods with sharp weapons of every kind, as the wind scatters rain-clouds.

sanskrit: te mahābāṇavarṣaiś ca śūlaiḥ prāsaiś ca dāruṇaiḥ pīḍyamānāḥ surāḥ sarve na vyatiṣṭhan samāhitāḥ
english: Afflicted by great showers of arrows, by dreadful spears and javelins, all the gods could not stand firm, however resolute.

sanskrit: tato vidrāvyamāṇeṣu tridaśeṣu sumālinā vasūnām aṣṭamo devaḥ sāvitro vyavatiṣṭhata
english: Then, as the thirty gods were being routed by Sumālī, the eighth of the Vasus, the god Sāvitra, stood his ground.

sanskrit: saṃvṛtaḥ svair anīkais tu praharantaṃ niśācaram vikrameṇa mahātejā vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Covered by his own troops, the great-souled one checked by his valour the night-wanderer who was striking in battle.

sanskrit: sumattayos tayor āsīd yuddhaṃ loke sudāruṇam sumālino vasoś caiva samareṣv anivartinoḥ
english: Between those two warriors, each of great valour — Sumālī and the Vasu — who never retreated in combat, a most dreadful battle took place in the world.

sanskrit: tatas tasya mahābāṇair vasunā sumahātmanā mahān sa pannagarathaḥ kṣaṇena vinipātitaḥ
english: Then the great-souled Vasu brought down in an instant that great serpent-chariot of Sumālī with his mighty arrows.

sanskrit: hatvā tu saṃyuge tasya rathaṃ bāṇaśataiḥ śitaiḥ gadāṃ tasya vadhārthāya vasur jagrāha pāṇinā
english: Having destroyed his chariot in battle with hundreds of sharp arrows, the Vasu seized a mace in his hand for the purpose of slaying him.

sanskrit: tāṃ pradīptāṃ pragṛhyāśu kāladaṇḍanibhāṃ śubhām tasya mūrdhani sāvitraḥ sumāler vinipātayat
english: Sāvitra quickly seized that blazing, auspicious mace resembling the staff of Death and brought it down upon Sumālī's head.

sanskrit: tasya mūrdhani solkābhā patantī ca tadā babhau sahasrākṣasamutsṛṣṭā girāv iva mahāśaniḥ
english: As it fell upon his head blazing like a meteor, it shone like a great thunderbolt hurled by the thousand-eyed Indra upon a mountain.

sanskrit: tasya naivāsthi kāyo vā na māṃsaṃ dadṛśe tadā gadayā bhasmasādbhūto raṇe tasmin nipātitaḥ
english: Neither his bones nor his body nor his flesh could be seen thereafter — struck down in that battle, he was reduced to ashes by the mace.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ saṃkhye rākṣasās te samantataḥ dudruvuḥ sahitāḥ sarve krośamānā mahāsvanam
english: Seeing him slain in battle, all those Rākṣasas fled on all sides together, wailing with a great cry.
